answer.rationale: The primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so the one decision this cycle must keep supply continuous. Deferral is not analogous to c5 (that case was non-critical and stayed month-to-month). A second source (c3) does not replace the expiring primary. Price reopen already failed, so another negotiate pass (c4/c6) is unlikely to land an 18% cut before expiry. Switching could cut unit cost if c2 still holds, but a full primary cutover in two weeks with no buffer would raise delivery risk and therefore TCO via line-down exposure. Renewing the incumbent (c1) keeps integration and deliveries intact; unit price stays high and the spend mandate is unmet—that residual cost and buffer risk is flagged, and c1/c2 need source checks before this is locked.
